# Introduction

Purpose

This SRS document describes the requirements for the proposed AI Integrated School Management and Communication Portal using Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) for SRIAAWP system. The primary purpose of this SRS is to provide a clear and comprehensive definition of the system’s capabilities and constraints. The SRS is intended for the stakeholders in SRIAAWP to review and confirm that the specified requirements accurately reflect their needs and expectations for the School Management and Communication Portal system. This document is also for the student and their respective supervisor to understand the scope of the project, guide the design and implementation of the system, and serve as a foundation for testing and validation.

Scope

In our proposed system, we are creating an efficient automated web-based School Management and Communication Portal system for the SRIAAWP school. We must improve the current manual workflow operations by removing the shortcomings of the existing system and by including different new features according to the needs of the stakeholders. The School Management and Communication Portal system is focused on being a web-based system since the stakeholder finds it more convenient and familiar to operate rather than being a mobile based application. The software product will allow teachers and staff to efficiently manage and retrieve official school documents, automatically manage events error-free, allows parents to quickly retrieve school memos and information, allows students to retrieve and submit their co-curricular achievements, and finally allows all users to query the AI chat assistant to promptly obtain information within the website.

The main benefits of this system towards our stakeholders include reducing resources used to search through information, saves time by providing an AI chatbot that gives instant support, reduces error by automating scheduling that can eliminate human error, enhances information accessibility ensuring important school notices do not go unnoticed, and linking students co-curricular information to the system to avoid outdated information. The objectives of this system follows the System Development Life Cycle (SDLC) starting with, to analyse the requirements of the administrative and communication requirements of the stakeholder, SRIAAWP. Following that, to design and develop a centralized web application for SRIAAWP including an administrative dashboard integrated with AI- powered RAG for teachers and an information dashboard integrated using a conflict-free calendar for parents. Finally, to test the system’s usability using suitable testing techniques, such as User Acceptance Testing (UAT), and User Experience Questionnaire (UEQ).

This SRS document provides a detailed description of the AI Integrated School Management and Communication Portal using RAG for SRIAAWP system. # Specific Requirements

User characteristics

The AI Integrated School Management and Communication Portal using Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) for SRIAAWP system will be used by four main types of users: Administrators / Head of Department, SRIAAWP Teachers / Staff, Parents, and SRIAAWP students.

Administrators / Head of Department

The administrators who will use the software are expected to have educational backgrounds relevant to administrative roles.

They may have varying levels of experience in managing school resources and handling administrative tasks.

They may have varying levels of technical expertise but are expected to be proficient in using common software web applications.

They will use the software to manage users, documents and other student related information.

SRIAAWP Teachers / Staff

The SRIAAWP teachers who will use the software are expected to have a minimum of a bachelor's degree in education and the respective field of interest.

They may have varying levels of technical expertise but are expected to be proficient in using common web applications.

They will use the software to access student records, modify and upload official documents, and manage new school events.

Parents

The parents who will use the software are expected to have basic computer skills, including familiarity with web-based applications.

They may have various different information that they want to know regarding their children’s academic information.

They will use the software to retrieve important school information and view their child’s academic information

SRIAAWP Students

The SRIAAWP students who will use the software are expected to have very little basic computer skills, including familiarity with mobile applications.

They will use the software to submit co-curricular achievements, and also retrieve important school information.

Some students may not have access to the web-application due to not having access to an electronic device.

All users can access the web-application without a need for registration, however personal information retrieval would require login/registration authorization.

All users can query the RAG based AI assistant to quickly retrieve school relevant information.

System Features

The AI Integrated School Management and Communication Portal using Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) for SRIAAWP system is a software system that operates on both computer devices and mobile devices, granted it has access to a modern web browser with internet access. The system provides a means for SRIAAWP Teachers and Staffs to better manage their official digital school documents, and allows error-free event management. Moreover, the system provides a way for parents and students to retrieve important school information including events, and also allows students to submit their co-curricular achievements for reviewing by their respective teachers. The system also implements an RAG based AI assistant to assist users in retrieving certain information quickly.

Use Case Details

UC01: Use Case Register/Login Account

**Table 3.1: Use Case Description for Register/Login Account**

| Use Case ID | UC01 |
| --- | --- |
| Use Case Name | Register/Login Account |
| Description | Allows users to create a new account or access the system using existing credentials. |
| Actor(s) | Administrator, Teacher/Staff, Parent, Student |
| Pre-condition(s) | User has access to the web portal. |
| Normal Flow(s)- NF | User selects Register or Login. User enters required credentials (Email, Password). System validates credentials. System redirects user to the appropriate dashboard based on role. |
| Alternative Flow(s) - AF | AF1 - Social Login  User selects "Login with Google " to authenticate using external providers. |
| Exception Flow(s) - EF | EF1 - Invalid Credentials System displays "Invalid Email or Password" and prompts the user to try again. |
| Post-condition(s) | User is authenticated and authorized to access specific system features. |

UC02: Use Case Reset Password

**Table 3.2: Use Case Description for Reset Password**

| Use Case ID | UC02 |
| --- | --- |
| Use Case Name | Reset Password |
| Description | Allows users to regain access to their account if they forget their password. |
| Actor(s) | Administrator, Teacher/Staff, Parent, Student |
| Pre-condition(s) | User has a registered email in the system. |
| Normal Flow(s)- NF | User clicks "Forgot Password". User enters registered email. System sends a reset link to the email. User enters a new password. |
| Exception Flow(s) - EF | EF1 - Email Not Found System informs the user that the email is not registered. EF2 - Expired Link If the user clicks the link after 24 hours, the system prompts for a new request. |
| Post-condition(s) | Password is updated in the database. |

UC03: Use Case Verify Registration

**Table 3.3: Use Case Description for Verify Registration**

| Use Case ID | UC03 |
| --- | --- |
| Use Case Name | Verify Registration |
| Description | A validation process to ensure the user identity before activating the account. |
| Actor(s) | Administrator, Teacher/Staff, Parent, Student |
| Pre-condition(s) | User has no account. |
| Normal Flow(s)- NF | User completes registration. System sends verification email. User clicks the verification link. |
| Exception Flow(s) - EF | EF1 - Invalid Token If the link is tampered with or expired, the system displays an error message. |
| Post-condition(s) | Account status is set to "Verified". |

UC04: Use Case Manage User & Roles

**Table 3.4: Use Case Description for Manage User & Roles**

| Use Case ID | UC04 |
| --- | --- |
| Use Case Name | Manage User & Roles |
| Description | The administrator manages user profiles and assigns roles (Teacher, Parent, etc.). |
| Actor(s) | Administrator |
| Pre-condition(s) | Administrator is logged in |
| Normal Flow(s)- NF | Admin accesses the User Management panel. Admin selects a user. Admin updates the role or status. |
| Exception Flow(s) - EF | EF1 - Last Admin Protection System prevents the admin from removing their own admin role if they are the only administrator left. |
| Post-condition(s) | User permissions are updated. |

| Post-condition(s) | Student record is updated for the semester. |

Performance and Other Requirements

Non-functional requirements describe how a system behaves, rather than just what tasks it can do. They focus on the quality of the system, like how fast it runs, how safe it is, and how easy it is to use. It is crucial to include these in the project plan to make sure the final product satisfies the users. According to ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148, these requirements are separated into three main categories: Software System Attributes, Performance and Other Requirements.

Software system attributes define the overall qualities of the software. They include the following:

**Usability:**

The website interface should have a modern and minimal look that includes helpful tooltips and first time user wizards/buttons to assist new users without need technical training.

**Reliability:**

The system must be available whenever the users need it, especially during busy periods like registration day.

**Maintainability:**

The code structure should be written clearly so that future developers can easily maintain the system and fix bugs or add new features.

**Portability:**

The system should work perfectly on any device running on any operating system (OS). It should be responsive to different screen sizes like mobile, phones, tablets, desktop computers.

**Compatibility:**

The system should be compatible and work smoothly across all modern web browsers like Chrome, Safari and Edge.

Performance requirements define the system’s capabilities to respond to user requests and handle data in a timely manner. These requirements include the following:

**Response Time:**

The system should retrieve pages and load in under 2 seconds, and the system should react to any user input within 3-5 seconds so that users do not feel they are waiting for too long.

**Throughput: **

The system should be able to handle user traffic at peak periods smoothly. For example, 200 parents log in at the same time to check on the week’s events.

**Capacity:**

The system needs enough storage space to keep years of school information, student records and teacher documents in the database.

**Availability:**

The system should aim for a 99% availability rate, to ensure users can access and check the calendar almost at any time.

Other requirements describe the non-functional requirements that do not fit under the categories mentioned above. These include the following:

**Security:**

The system should only authorize logged in users to access certain parts of the system. It should use Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) to validate users to certain actions.

**Safety:**

The system must automatically backup files and records to the database, if possible, on a daily basis to avoid missing data.

**Legal and Regulatory:**

The system must get parental and user consent before storing personal data or student photos.

**Environmental:**

The system reduces the usage of papers and physical documents because it digitizes and automates such manual processes.

Design Constraints

Design Constraints explain constraints given by the organization where the software product will be used. This includes certain organizational standard and other external non-functional requirements.

Environmental constraints:

A major design constraint is that the system must be developed and hosted using low-cost or free-tier services and optimized so it does not exceed these limits.

Hardware constraints:

The system must be designed to be able to run on a minimum of 8GB of RAM which is the standard recommendation for modern web applications.

Security constraints:

The system should not store passwords using plain texts and should uses Supabase to hash and secure them.

Compatibility constraints:

The system should be designed to be compatible with Windows 10 or equivalent OS.
